question: Should Gateway allow scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and should that syntax live inside `allowedOrigins` or a separate constrained pattern field?
rationale: This issue changes the Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary; the source failure is clear, but automation should not choose the permanent wildcard grammar or security posture.

options.title: Define constrained pattern contract
options.body: Add a narrow reviewed pattern grammar with schema/docs/audit/tests and then implement only that approved wildcard surface.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Continue with exact opaque-origin fixes and decline scheme wildcards as too broad for Gateway origin authorization.

options.title: Allow Chrome-extension wildcard in place
options.body: Permit `chrome-extension://*` inside `allowedOrigins`, but require scheme-specific matching and negative security tests before merge.

recommendation.title: Define constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow reviewed pattern grammar with schema/docs/audit/tests and then implement only that approved wildcard surface.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the Gateway browser-origin policy and merged the existing global wildcard behavior.
